FINDER: BOUND THE SELECTED-ARCHETYPE DEEP PAGE. PAGE THE 10,000-ROW WINDOW BY KEY BEFORE READING system_search DETAILS. OWNER-APPROVED API QUERY DELTA (2026-10-31), WITH NO CHANGE TO RESULTS, ORDER, RESPONSE SHAPE OR RANKING IDENTITY.

CHANGE ONLY: apps/api/src/ranking/ranking_sql.py (the selected-archetype page query `_picked_page_query` and its comments only), tests/test_ranking_sql.py, tests/test_archetype_rankings_v3.py, and CHANGES.md. Change scripts/v3_archetype_plan_probe.py, its tests, or any pinned operator or identity digest ONLY if a test proves that the new SQL shape requires it, and then explain each change in your summary. DO NOT CHANGE: `_picked_count_query`, the no-pick (Any) queries, `build_ranked_query`'s validation, apps/api/src/ranking/profile.py, apps/api/src/routers/archetypes.py, apps/api/src/models.py, any migration, any response field, RANKING_VERSION or `ranking_sha256()`, any workflow, or any other file.

EVIDENCE (Finder F4 slice 1c, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f4-archetype-ui-design.md sections 7 and 8): a PostgreSQL 18 proof on 1,000,000 systems, saturating every window and running every archetype at the B/A/S floors under `plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan`, measured 24 of 24 passes for the first page (2–4 ms warm, 7–21 ms cold, against 300 / 1,500 ms) and 24 of 24 for the bounded count (38–67 ms warm, 63–185 ms cold, against 600 / 2,500 ms). It measured 24 of 24 FAILURES for the near-ceiling page (offset 9950, page size 50): 705–1,098 ms warm against 600 ms, with the same result under production's planner settings (effective_cache_size 128 GB, work_mem 32 MB). The cause is the `ranked_page` CTE. It joins all 10,000 window rows to `v3_app.system_search` and selects `s.*` before `LIMIT/OFFSET`, so for a deep offset the planner needs 10,000 joined detail rows. It chose a Hash Join over a Seq Scan of the whole system_search table (1,000,000 rows, about 650 ms), then sorted 10,000 wide rows. The count query's join is the same, but it reads no search columns, so it runs as a nested loop of Index Only Scans on system_search_pkey (10,001 loops, about 45 ms). Production's 2026-10-23 publication plan probe measured only offset-0 pages and counts, never a deep page.

THE CHANGE: keep `archetype_window` exactly as it is (the partial-index window with its literal floor, ORDER BY and LIMIT 10000). Then:
(1) A new keys-only stage that joins the window to `v3_app.system_search` exactly as the count query joins it: the same view, the same `ON <alias>.system_id64 = aw.system_id64`, and the same `WHERE <alias>.derived_generation_id = <pin>` via `_pinned()`. It selects only `aw.system_id64` and `aw.selected_archetype_weighted_e4` and no search column, so that membership in the published search generation filters the window exactly as today (an inner join on a unique key: a window row without a search row is still excluded before paging, so page contents and offsets cannot shift). It then does ORDER BY `selected_archetype_weighted_e4 DESC, system_id64 ASC` and LIMIT $limit OFFSET $offset with the existing two parameters.
(2) A detail stage that joins only those page keys back to `v3_app.system_search` (pinned the same way) for `s.*`, plus the page key's `selected_archetype_weighted_e4`.
(3) The final `picked` fetch and the final ORDER BY, unchanged.

Use a distinct alias for each system_search reference, keep the final fetch alias `picked` (the plan probe asserts it), keep the params list `[limit, offset]`, and update the comments to explain the stages and why the details come after the page. The rows, their order, every column and every value must be identical to today's query for every valid limit/offset.

  - the detail join comes after it and has no LIMIT of its own;
  - `s.*` is selected only in the detail stage;

Embed the old query as a test-local string copied from the current code: same rows, same order, same columns.
